catalog_quote: ... ni en ki geschreven . Het intensiteitsaccent wordt niet aangeduid . Voor het substan- tief valt het op de eerste kernklinker indien hij hoogtonig is . Is hij laagtonig, dan wordt het prefix beklemtoond zo er een is . In de gevallen met (n-) prefix wordt de eerste kernklinker beklemtoond . Enkele voorbeelden met het intensiteitsaccent: d'ikama voet; g'ulandúlá volgen; k'u'tú schorpioen; ŋg'undú beek- tuin, mv . m'angundu . Er zijn vijf goed onderscheiden tonen, die met de volgende noten van het harmonium konden vergeleken worden: a, de overhoge toon á, de hoge å, de middelhoge à, de lage ä, de overlage mi (e) re (d) do kruis do (c) ... [p. 267] ... klinker lang, dan wordt hij behandeld als uit twee tijden bestaande; de eerste tijd heeft de overhoge toon, de tweede tijd behoudt de eigen toon van de klinker: kűùtú, het is een schorpioen, (kutú schorpioen) ...

new_statements.translation: ... here ni and ki are written. The intensity accent [stress] is not marked. For the noun it falls on the first root vowel if that vowel is high-toned. If it is low-toned, then the prefix is stressed, if there is one. In the cases with the (n-) prefix the first root vowel is stressed. Some examples with the intensity accent: d'ikama 'foot'; g'ulandúlá 'to follow'; kutú 'scorpion'; ŋg'undú 'brook-garden', pl. m'angundu. There are five well-distinguished tones, which could be compared with the following notes of the harmonium: a̋ the extra-high tone, á the high, å the mid-high, à the low, ä the extra-low ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: Mbagani is a tone language (Van Coillie hears five surface pitch levels and gives lexical and grammatical tone rules). Word stress ('intensiteitsaccent') is tone-conditioned and sits at the left edge of the word: in nouns (including class-15 infinitives such as gu-landúlá) it falls on the stem-initial syllable when that syllable is high-toned; when the stem-initial syllable is low-toned the syllabic CV class prefix carries the stress instead (dí-kama, má-ngundu); nouns whose only prefix is the non-syllabic nasal N- stress the stem-initial syllable regardless (ngúndu). Stress is not written in the orthography.
new_statements.exceptions: Nasal-prefix (n-) nouns: stress on first root vowel even if low-toned (prefix cannot bear it). Rule is stated for the noun ('voor het substantief'); no separate statement for finite verbs was found in part 2 (1949).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (isolated nouns/infinitives as cited); stress explicitly distinguished from the five-level tone system described in the same paragraph. Text obtained as page-numbered scanned snippets from Google Books snippet view (three overlapping snippets of p.261), not from a full scan; wording should be re-checked against the printed page.
new_statements.identity_note: Van Coillie describes the Mbagani of the Bambágání/Babíndzí around Tshibala mission, territoire de Luisa, Kasai (his own 'Taalkaart van het gewest Luisa', p.259) = Binji/Mbagani [bpj], Glottolog binj1249 (Mbagani-Lwalwa < Luban). Not to be confused with the 'Babindi' south of Mpanya Mutombo / Babindi of Muetshi, whose speech Stappers 1952 and Burssens 1954 class as a Tshiluba (luba1249) dialect; the Lubumbashi 'langue bindi' mémoires may refer to the latter. ASJP's L22_MBAGANI list is (mis)keyed to song1303 because older Ethnologue editions listed Mbagani as a Songe dialect.

tone.says: Unknown beyond the report that it is a tonology sketch by a professional Bantu tonologist (author of the Tshiluba and Songye tonologies); Stappers 1952 adds that Mbagani deviates strongly from Tshiluba in 'phonologie en tonologie'. Would be the only trained-linguist tone analysis of Mbagani before Tshibola 1985.

sources.note: Describes another variety (Glottolog mbag1238). Gives an overview of the synchronic phonology incl. the tone system; 'At the tone level, Cibinji cya ngusu has completely inverted the tone scheme of Proto Bantu so that inherited high tones became low tones, and low tones are realized as high tones' - i.e. a two-tone (H/L) system with Luba-type tone reversal. Says nothing about Mbagani L22 tone.
